items.objective: Find B3, C4 and D4 on string 2, frets 0, 1 and 3.
Compare B3–C4 with B3–C#4: one fret and two frets from the same starting note.
Play C4–D4–E4–D4–C4 on string 2, frets 1–3–5–3–1, shifting the hand gently.
Place a silent beat after D4; count through it before E4, then return to C4.
Play the eight-beat phrase, then make another with C4, D4, E4, one rest and a final C4.
Move the question to G3–A3–B3 on string 3, frets 0–2–4.
Compare E4 on string 1 open and string 2 fret 5, then G4 at 1:3 and 2:8.
Play C4–D4 on string 2 and E4–F4 on string 1, then return.
Play the single notes C4–E4–G4; these outline C major without a sustained stretch.
Compare the same opening ending on C4 or G4 over an imagined C chord.
Build sixteen beats with an opening, a counted rest and a final C4, using both strings.
Play the same phrase once connected and once with gently separated notes.
Place A1 on beat one of each four-beat bar, then count the silence.
Alternate A1 and E2, two beats each, keeping the fifth quieter than the root.
Compare one-beat A1 with two-beat A1, stopping precisely when the rest begins.
Support one bar of A minor then one bar of D minor: roots A1 and D2 start each bar.
Accompany Am–Dm–G–Am with roots on beat one and fifths on beat three; finish with a rest.
Try D2 on the and of beat four before repeating it on the next downbeat.
Find C4 next to the pair of black keys; place right-hand fingers 1–5 on C4–G4.
Play C4–D4–E4–G4–F4–E4–D4–C4 with right-hand fingers 1–2–3–5–4–3–2–1.
Leave a beat of silence after D4 and after G4, releasing the keys without pedal.
Add left-hand C3 under the first C4 and G3 under F4 in bar two; let the right hand carry the melody.
Play four bars with left-hand roots C3–F3–G3–C3 and a right-hand melody that ends on C4.
Let the left hand play C4–D4–E4 while the right adds C5, then G4, as light support.
Play open strings G4–C4–E4–A4 in course order: the fourth string is higher than C4.
Fret string 1 at fret 3 and play each course before a gentle C strum.
Use gentle downstrokes on C and leave counted silent beats between them.
Play E4–F4–G4 on string 2, then open A4 on string 1 and return.
Alternate a short melody with one C chord; use the pause to prepare string 1 fret 3.
Compare open string 4 G4 with string 2 fret 3 G4; both have the same pitch.
Play open G3–D4–A4–E5; each displayed course represents two physical strings tuned together.
On the D course play frets 0–2–4–5 with alternating down and up strokes, then return.
Play D4–F#4 on the D course and A4–B4 on the A course, then return.
Hear D4–F#4–A4 separately; then play open D4, open A4 and F#5 at E-course fret 2 as a D chord.
Make sixteen beats with a D4 opening, one crossing to the A course, counted silence and a final D4.
Give D4 two even eighth-note attacks before the phrase; use a relaxed down-up pair.
